http_semantics.note: The triggering request produced NO HTTP response at any status level: the server closed the connection mid-request (requests raises RemoteDisconnected -> runtime status=0) and the process was then unreachable on /healthz for two retries. This is not a 2xx-with-business-code case; the failure sits below the HTTP semantics layer (process death), which is itself the constraint's forbidden outcome.

Grep for 'too many shards|max_shard|upper bound' across the clone: the only hit is a test-file comment (lib/collection/tests/integration/common/mod.rs:18 'Test collections for this upper bound of shards.') — no production guard exists. Contrast: replication_factor is explicitly clamped to known peers at shard_distribution.rs:88 (cmp::min), which is why the live probes with replication_factor=4294967295 and write_consistency_factor=4294967295 returned 200 with the service alive.
